Avedon Director Ron Howard On Richard Avedon’s “Creative Courage,” and His Favorite Images From 'In the American West'

Tanggal: 09 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.vanityfair.com/photos/ron-howard-richard-avedon-documentary

Sebagaimana diketahui, in his new documentary avedon, director ron howard traces the vivid legacy of the influential photographer richard avedon, which premieres november 11 on netflix. “The subjects he worked with on the commercial side of his career were dazzling and beautiful, and he was so entertaining and expressive in the way that he would shoot them. But I really had no idea how he applied his status, his influence, his access to tell this other kind of story about human beings that was honest, insightful, and more journalistic,” Howard tells Vanity Fair.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the glamorous heights of avedon’s career were what first caught howard’s attention. Later, he realized a few of his favorite portraits were taken by Avedon. Then it was even his TV commercials, like Brooke Shields [in Calvin Klein ads],” Howard said. It’s not against a white background…” notes Howard. It so captured the foundational strength of character and intelligence that Kareem carried with him along with his basketball talent. “I know Kareem a little bit. One of these was a portrait of a young Kareem Abdul-Jabbar at a playground in New York holding a basketball “and kind of casually standing there looking straight into the camera. “I became aware of him really in the ’80s. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, initially, howard, who spent three years making the film, thought it was going to be more focused on the fashion and celebrity worlds that avedon inhabited. However, his fascination with photographs like “sad Marilyn” (Avedon’s 1957 portrait of Marilyn Monroe) grew into a respect for the full breadth of Avedon’s career, and his “creative courage as an artist. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa in the film, footage of avedon and new interviews with lauren hutton, tina brown, adam gopnik, hilton als, joel meyerowitz, larry gagosian, and avedon’s son john, among others, paint a picture of a driven, curious, and sometimes mercurial artist. In the 1950s, Avedon’s career took off when he began shooting for Harper’s Bazaar, Vogue, and Vanity Fair. Eventually, he ventured into documentary assignments and more political subjects, including Nothing Personal (1964), a photobook with text by James Baldwin that captured the tensions of the Civil Rights era alongside a broader look at American life, a three panel portrait of anti-war protesters the Chicago Seven, and members of America’s political and financial elite at the time of the country’s bicentennial (“The Family”) for Rolling Stone. He injected a sense of play and prewar European glamour into his images by drawing inspiration from the films of Fred Astaire and Ginger Rogers. At the height of his career, he seemingly shifted quite easily from photographing celebrities to documenting anti-war protests and the counterculture of the 1960s, even when his work was met with mixed reactions.

Dovima with elephants, evening dress by Dior, Cirque d’Hiver, Paris, August 1955.

James Baldwin, New York, January 9, 1963.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, avedon (left) with gloria vanderbilt and sidney lumet at a party for the movie premiere of east of eden (dir. Elia Kazan), 1955.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “we tried to reflect the risks he took and the transitions he made with his art and his career,” howard shares. He wasn’t on assignment initially… he just committed. Had Howard made the documentary in Avedon’s lifetime, he would have liked to have asked him directly about the turning points in his career. “In all the interviews, he just kind of made it seem like it was a natural step. But to me, it's not a natural step to stop getting thousands and thousands of dollars an hour to shoot commercials and shoot for the world's most read magazines, and go to Vietnam where no one was really. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in 1979, the amon carter museum of american art in fort worth, texas, commissioned avedon to capture a portrait of the west. He worked on this ambitious portfolio periodically through 1984, traveling across 17 states like California, Colorado, Iowa, North Dakota, Texas, and Wyoming, with assistants and a researcher, Laura Wilson, who helped Avedon arrange 752 portrait sittings. (Wilson also documented the making of the project in her own remarkable photographs and writing. The result was In the American West—a turning point in Avedon’s career. ) In total, Avedon printed 124 photographs (some as large as four feet tall) and exhibited them at the museum in 1985. Prior to the project’s completion, in 1983, Vanity Fair ran five photographs from the eventual series, showing coal miners covered in dust and one lone oil worker alongside a feature on Wagner’s operas and an excerpt of Gabriel García Márquez’s Chronicle of a Death Foretold.

Berdasarkan laporan, “one of the reasons i was drawn to [in the american west] is because my family roots are in the midwest,” howard says. “I see a lot of truth in these images. ”.

Avedon conducting a portrait session for In the American West beside his 8x10 camera.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in a similar fashion to august sander’s massive undertaking people of the 20th century, avedon went looking for “men and women who work at hard, uncelebrated jobs, the people who are often ignored or overlooked,” wilson wrote. In doing so he joined a whole legion of photographers whose images have come to define broad swaths of middle and western America. I don’t think the West of these portraits is any more conclusive than the West of John Wayne. But unlike common readings of Sander’s project at the time, Avedon was clear that his version of the West was totally subjective, more of a cinematic panorama than an objective record. He was emphatic that all photographs are filtered through the photographer’s eye, and become their interpretation. Through Wilson, he declared, “This is a fictional West. ”.

Below, Howard reflects on five of his favorite photographs from Avedon’s In the American West.

Diungkapkan bahwa “i asked if that was makeup, and i was assured that none of it was. I mean, wow, this is what these workers look like. This is what was in their lungs and their pores. I have cousins and uncles who worked in the oil fields. [Avedon] set up, and just as workers were coming off their shift, he was getting them in front of the camera. I never had any idea that they had their days looking like they’d been through what this guy has been through on his shift. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “the boy with the rattlesnake was the first photo that [avedon] took where he knew he was going to get at something deeper. It is also featured in the documentary because it was the proof in [Avedon’s] mind that he was going to be able to identify moments and individuals that would be arresting and mean a lot on an artistic level. My own dad, to try to get some spending money [in the ’30s], was hunting and trapping raccoons to sell skins to the junk dealer or possums they could eat. It also speaks of that region as a very pragmatic region. [The subject] was a teenager. He felt like this was almost religious iconography in a way, or mythic. Absolutely just a pragmatic way of life there. As Avedon says, he's a boy turning into a man, and here he's doing this kind of work, so it speaks to a transformation. So that image always resonated with me. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, “the beekeeper is, of course, a stunning image–one that doesn't have that much to do with the american west. I think [Avedon] could have found somebody like that in almost any corner of the planet, but it certainly is fascinating and a tribute to the research team that was working with him to help find him. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, “the maintenance worker who’s dressed up in a really flashy suit, suit jacket, tie and hat, that just looks very familiar to me. I mean, the jacket and all the embroidery on it, the flowers, I never saw anything like that with my family. This guy looks like he could be a country western singer or could be trying to be a country western star. That looks like a hardworking guy getting dressed up on the weekend. But the hat, the tie, the gaze, the posture looks very, very familiar to me. They didn’t have that kind of flourish. ”.

#243. Elon Musk’s Cybertruck Is Dumb, Ugly, and Mercifully Dead

📅 09 Nov 2026

Elon Musk’s Cybertruck Is Dumb, Ugly, and Mercifully Dead

Tanggal: 09 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.vanityfair.com/story/cybertruck-appraisal

Diungkapkan bahwa in march 2024, a tesla cybertruck speeding down sunset boulevard slammed head-on into the beverly hills hotel’s iconic entrance sign just before midnight. Passersby winding through the Flats slowed down to watch as Elon Musk’s statue to his own insecurities—the stainless-steel embodiment of nuance-free American ego—demolished in front of Hollywood’s unofficial canteen.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, every decade gets the iconography it deserves. At just about the midpoint of the 2020s, ours had arrived, fully formed.

Diungkapkan bahwa and now the cybertruck is dead, which is wonderful news. Musk, who’s having a historically bad November, announced late last week that Tesla will be “winding down” production of the Cybertruck around mid-2027, putting an end to the most hated car in America. And it’s not entirely due to anti-Elon sentiment: Tesla’s general sales have been relatively steady, going down a bit as Musk went full DOGE mode in 2025 before rebounding in 2026. People like Elon’s cars. I was going to call it the most polarizing car in America, but honestly, no one likes this thing. They just do not like the Cybertruck.

Diungkapkan bahwa true, its death has been mourned by some—especially the self-selecting devotees who installed bulletproof glass in their cybertrucks before shooting them with rifles. These people exist. But mostly, the news has been greeted with a rush of enthusiasm, relief, and, more than anything else, blue-pilled schadenfreude.

Now would be the right moment in the news cycle for an art writer such as myself to make a contrarian argument: that the Cybertruck was secretly a design masterpiece—some kind of neo-Donald Judd breakthrough unleashed ahead of its time.

Berdasarkan laporan, i am not going to make that argument, because that is not true. No one in the future will look back on the Cybertruck as an unheralded art object. It looks like a birdhouse designed by Zaha Hadid, which I would love to have as a vessel for feeding hungry birds at my (sadly hypothetical) Zaha Hadid house. Not even close. It’s The Jetsons for meatheads, a Batmobile for people who secretly root for the Joker. But I would not want it as a vehicle to park in a driveway. It is a bad car.

Sebagaimana diketahui, and yet, that crashed cybertruck in front of the beverly hills hotel is seared into my brain, playing on repeat like the most unsubtle lana del rey song ever written. It’s a decade that wound through four years of a former president denying the lawful election of a current president, only to see that former president return to power. Even beyond that crash, the Cybertruck is the ultimate symbol of this surreal and cruel decade, one that started with a global pandemic and a government suggesting the possibility of a bleach injection as treatment. Through it all, we’ve sunk deeper into our collective psychosis—one that’s forced us into rooms with our devices, addicted to social media and artificial intelligence, consuming half-real information and spewing it back out into the world.

It’s a perfect world for the Tesla Cybertruck to define.

The Cybertruck arrived right at the dawn of the decade, in what we can now see as a completely different timeline.

Berdasarkan laporan, musk unveiled the car in november 2019 at tesla’s design studio. Head designer Franz von Holzhausen attempted to demonstrate the vehicle’s shatterproof glass by hurtling a metal ball at a window at full speed. The window shattered. Great omen! It was also pretty weird that Musk was introduced by a hologram of someone called “Cybergirl,” who people speculated was actually a hologram of Grimes, the pop star Musk was dating at the time.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, plenty of design press fawned over the shiny new thing—“long live the cybertruck. See you in the Thunderdome,” wrote Dwell. But Wired wisely asked the opinion of an actual expert: Raphael Zammit, who chairs transportation design at Motor City’s own College for Creative Studies.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “i was like, ‘oh my goodness! what did tesla do? what did they do?” he said. It’s what we tell them not to do. “It literally breaks every rule we tell to our students. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, regardless, the cybertruck started to infiltrate the cultural atmosphere. It was embraced, very early, by rappers. It was lampooned on The Simpsons. There were countless memes. Weeks after the unveiling, Travis Scott used his personal connections to the Tesla CEO (they did Christmas together with the Kardashian-Jenners) to snag a Cybertruck for his video for “Gang Gang,” a posse cut with the Cactus Jack crew.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, three years later, pharrell williams, 21 savage, and tyler, the creator featured the cybertruck in their video for “cash in, cash out”—rendered in claymation. Bad Bunny said, “Me monté en la Cybertruck y me acordé de la Montero de los viejos tiempo. Offset’s video for “Swing My Way” has Anok Yai sitting atop a Cybertruck. ” Meek Mill said, “They was doing cyber attacks, so I bought a Cybertruck. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa the cars fascinated artists too. These artists were certainly taking a critical eye toward the Cybertruck, but for some art collectors, there was nothing ironic about it. I recall with great happiness the perverse thrill of Frieda Toranzo Jaeger’s Cybertruck, a painting in her 2022 show at MoMA PS1. Julia Wachtel’s CyberChrist, on view at Todd Von Ammon’s DC gallery, von ammon co, earlier this year, pictures Jesus Christ pulling an elongated Cybertruck behind him. At least, a specific kind of collector. When I arrived at the convention center for Art Basel Miami Beach in 2024, the first full year of Cybertruck distribution, there was a line of Cybertrucks wrapped around the block.

Berdasarkan laporan, but that’s the thing about the cybertruck: there was always more supply than demand. According to automotive data platform Kelley Blue Book, Tesla moved nearly 39,000 of them in 2024, a decent start. Musk initially hoped to sell 250,000 units per year. In 2025, sales dropped, then dropped again in 2026.

Sebagaimana diketahui, perhaps the cybertruck could have endured the ridicule of design experts, car enthusiasts, and aesthetes with even just a whiff of good taste if it weren’t for the massive backlash that accompanied musk’s move into radical right-wing politics, and his full-throated support of donald trump. No one stepped in to intervene. The cars got defaced. Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, fisherwoman (olivia colman) has always been an outcast in her town. She has no real friends and not much of a romantic prospect. Diungkapkan bahwa he loves deeply and purely, without constraining how his wife should live. Sadly, this nonconforming spirit also makes the Fisherwoman doubt his love and fidelity. She has seen the men of this society. She finds it hard to believe that she has one who respects and loves her.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i left wicker very annoyed with the fisherwoman. She almost killed her husband because of a lie. It’s also clear that he only exists for her. Diungkapkan bahwa however, then i had to think about how many women and men let their lack of self-esteem or past trauma ruin good things in their lives. Many relationships have been destroyed because one or both people in them let their insecurities grow and create bigger problems. The Fisherwoman is frustrating, but she’s very human.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i really enjoyed the wicker ending because everyone got what they deserved. The townsfolk got scammed and traumatized. The Butcher (Phil Daniels ) got murdered, as the worst husband of them all, and the Fisherwoman and Wicker Husband left with a new child.

Berdasarkan laporan, it was only after the fisherwoman could let go of her insecurities and her awful town that she could have a happy ending. Wicker is about letting love into your life, even when you don’t think you deserve it.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the fisherwoman creates a husband who loves her completely, but she also learns to love herself in the process. Find love within yourself, and the right person may find you, or you will at least love yourself enough to feel fulfilled with or without a partner. That’s the real message. Wicker is definitely worth seeing in a theater full of women, or alone, where you can meditate on its messages.

Either way, come for the sexy parts, stay for the self-love.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “rip dolly smoky mountain angel” was one of the first signs we saw as we pulled up on the side of a motel in pigeon forge, tennessee. This was in early October. I am not the kind of person who cries over celebrity deaths, but after I heard that she died, I went to my closet to find a Dolly Parton T-shirt I had bought the one time I saw her live, at a concert of mostly acoustic songs in Queens in 2016. I couldn’t find it. Just down the same road was another memorial to her on a Burger King sign. Dolly Parton, the country singer and actor, widely considered a Great American Who Everyone Loves, had died, at the age of 80, in late August. I blamed my brief flirtation with the Marie Kondo method, but there was no way that T-shirt hadn’t sparked joy.

Berdasarkan laporan, early october in sevier county, in far eastern tennessee, where parton was born, is full of cabins on some parcels of land that dot the ancient appalachians. The Great Smoky Mountains National Park draws masses about 13 miles from Dollywood. But among the rolling green expanses are Mexican supermarkets, coffee shops, apple orchards, and pumpkin patches. This is where she opened the amusement park Dollywood in 1986. The fancier of my friends identified the area as where the Blackberry Farm resort is. But Pigeon Forge has a feeling of a Jersey Shore boardwalk in Appalachia, with a strip of businesses that sell vapes and ATV rides and Moon Pies a block from a Margaritaville hotel.

Sebagaimana diketahui, parton opened dollywood in 1986 at the foothills of the great smoky mountains. Today, it draws in millions of people annually—loving fans who don her iconic pink cowboy hat or accessories honoring the park's famous Grist Mill Cinnamon Bread (a cult favorite).

Diungkapkan bahwa locals heap the kind of praise on parton that we’ve come to expect knowing her reputation as a goddess among mortals. “I got to meet her three times at the park because she would just show up and stand there with a crowd of people. For someone who’s been famous as long as she’s been famous you’d expect a certain air of haughtiness,” he says. “People don’t understand what she did for this place and meant to this place. She threw lots of money at it and went out of her way to take care of this place,” an Uber driver named Eric told me as we exited the highway into Dollywood, with its script logo and “love every moment” greeting signs. “But I was stunned at how kind she was. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, parton’s job title at the park was dreamer-in-chief, and part of dollywood’s allure is that it’s a shrine to her life and career. There’s a replica of the two-room wood cabin where she grew up a sharecropper’s daughter, in close quarters alongside her parents and 10 siblings. (The original home still stands about 10 miles away but isn’t open to the public. Her home, not even 500 square feet, had no electricity nor running water. ).

Berdasarkan laporan, parton wrote the country ballad “i will always love you” in 1973 as a heartfelt farewell to her longtime business partner porter wagoner. Now, fans honoring Dolly's memory have used the slogan for the park's new annual festival, which opens in March 2027.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, that modest beginning is plenty known, but dollywood also celebrates parton as she became a household name and wildly rich. It has a gallery devoted to her Imagination Library, which has donated more than 300 million books to children around the world. Another building across a landscaped path celebrates her role in the workplace revenge comedy 9 to 5 (September 25 has now been christened a holiday in Sevier County) and houses a half dozen of her wigs, sorted by decade, all platinum, all voluminous. Parton’s costumes are scattered around the tributes, including a black flared jumpsuit with a hot pink shirt and neck ruffle so intense it looks Elizabethan. A plaque commemorates her wig stylists, starting with her Aunt Colleen. The Dolly Parton Experience is a museum devoted to her trajectory, from Nashville ingenue to a celebrity among celebrities (photos show her with Mick Jagger in the ’60s and Whitney Houston in the ’90s). Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, some park employees have not fared well without parton. One tour guide admits: “Today is the first day I haven’t cried. " Parton passed away on August 25 at the age of 80 after a battle with cancer.

Horses with cowboys and cowgirls astride them jump through rings of fire, someone does wire work while dangling from the ceiling, and American flags fly in abundance. For dinner, we hit the 8:30 show of Dolly Parton’s Stampede in Pigeon Forge, an equestrian version of dinner theater where guests are served a whole chicken, pulled pork, corn, greens, a biscuit, pie, and unlimited soda, all to be eaten by hand while the not so vague perfume of manure wafts through the air. We catch a pig race. ” I squeal as a few actual buffalo take the arena. “There’s a reason I stick to horses. Sooo-ey! At another point, a volunteer from the audience disappears from a barrel before our eyes. After the show, I ask a cowboy how the majestic creatures are as animal coworkers, and he shakes his head. Even in the perfect bubble of Dollywood, in the wake of her death, Parton’s spirit has already faded into the nostalgia.

Every single one replies that their trip has been planned long before. Berdasarkan laporan, the butterfly is a key part of dollywood's logo, representing parton's personal emblem. She cemented the motif into her career in 1974 with the hit song, “Love is Like a Butterfly. As a little girl growing up in the Smoky Mountains, she was fascinated by butterflies and related to their gentle grace. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, maybe, i say to dondre, no one will talk to me because i, unlike about 50% of the people there, am not wearing a t-shirt emblazoned with a bible verse, a military slogan, or a celebration of america’s 250 years. Maybe what made Dolly Parton so winning—her apparent lack of judgment—is not something I inherently have. I keep pointing out paintings of crosses and eagles and American flags—often all combined on one canvas together—for sale. It can’t hurt to try to be a little more like Parton in our own daily lives.

Diungkapkan bahwa maybe she had an optimism no one can ever replace. And that’s ultimately okay because you can try to channel that anywhere. Even in the perfect bubble of Dollywood, in the wake of her death, Parton’s spirit has already faded into the nostalgia, a curio like Graceland, but with a vintage steam train ride.

Berdasarkan laporan, i succumb and buy a christmas ornament with parton dressed as santa and eat a chicken salad sandwich served on a butterfly-logo-shaped pretzel. I guess I enjoy Dollywood the way I enjoy going dancing in Berlin gay clubs or karaoke birthday parties: It is an experience, and a fun one, but not what I would choose. Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, awards season will be here before we know it, and there are already a few projects getting early buzz. One of them is the new A24 movie Club Kid, which stars Jordan Firstman, who also wrote and directed the acclaimed dramedy. Club Kid is my favorite movie of the year, largely thanks to its heart and the authentic representation of queer nightlife. I had to ask him about bringing those sequences together, and he got honest about why the club scenes (especially in the darkroom) went so hard.

Berdasarkan laporan, club kid is a new lgbtq+ movie, and as a gay man myself i was immediately take by how real those club scenes felt. As you can see in the video above, I asked Firstman about how he brought those sequences together, especially the scene where his character Peter has sex with a woman in a club darkroom. He told me:.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i got in like a fight with someone because they're like 'darkrooms like didn't come until like 2019. But I do feel like, you know, Chris Cruse started this party Spotlight in LA, which was kind of like our first like LA introduction into darkrooms. It was a cool moment for queer people because we like weren't like doing that publicly before really in my generation. But I say like the Berlin-ification of New York, mama, in the movie. ' And I was like, 'They definitely came in 2016. ' I like remember like at least they were popping up in New York, but I remember going to like a sex party in 2015 or 16. So yeah, it was important for me to like show that and show what goes down at the club.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, for those unfamiliar, darkrooms have a long history in queer history. They're typically pitch black rooms in bars where patrons can engage in anonymous sexual activity. They were shown in the media dating back to Harvey Fierstein's Torch Song Trilogy back in 1988, and Jordan Firstman's movie brings them back to the big screen in a more modern context.

Diungkapkan bahwa in a drug-fueled haze peter has sex with a woman early in club kid in a darkroom, and that unknowingly gets her pregnant. That's how his son Arlo ends up dropped at his door over a decade later, with the party promoter suddenly forced to become a parent to a child he never knew existed.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, there's been a ton of chatter lately about lgbtq+ movies actually starring queer actors, and jordan firstman was able to bring a very real, niche experience to the mainstream as the director, writer, and star of club kid. Later in our conversation he spoke more about the way the darkroom scene was shot, telling me:.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but i think also showing it in a elegant way, like i really love how that scene is shot. I think it's like very classy. And it's not, it's like, I don't know. It just it's like beautiful, but still it does, a dark room does feel that way.

Berdasarkan laporan, he's not wrong. The darkroom scene isn't a sexually explicit scene, despite the setting. Instead it uses light in a fascinating way that's immersive, but not overly graphic. The audience sees Peter decide to have sex with a woman at the behest of a guy he's interested in, and it's that union that serves as the catalyst for the movie's primary story.

Diungkapkan bahwa the authentic way the darkroom is shown, as well as the unique chaos of the nightlife as a whole, instantly brings club kid into a specific time and place. The movie shows what the club scene is like for LGBTQ+ folks, warts and all. While it's a world not all moviegoers might understand, the specificity of Firstman's work ends up making the story universal.

Berdasarkan laporan, club kid is in select theaters now as part of the 2026 movie release list, and will be getting more screenings as the month goes on. I laughed, I cried, and I loved how real the movie felt as a member of the queer community.

Sebagaimana diketahui, however, i get the sneaking suspicion anyone watching the macy’s thanksgiving day parade won’t have any trouble spotting earl. That’s because he’s going to be 30. 5 feet wide. 4 feet tall and 14. Literally, you won’t be able to miss him.

Diungkapkan bahwa reviews have dropped for how to rob a bank, starring nicholas hoult, zoë kravitz, pete davidson, anna sawai, and john c. Reilly, and they aren’t pretty. The movie, directed by David Leitch (Deadpool 2, The Fall Guy), hits the 2026 movie schedule this week. The reviews are not as uniformly negative as they were for another Amazon MGM movie, 2025’s War of the Worlds (How to Rob a Bank is hovering just south of 50% on Rotten Tomatoes), but they are giving me the same vibes. That’s not a good thing.

Berdasarkan laporan, even in some of the more positive reviews, writers aren’t impressed by the heist movie’s seemingly ham-fisted attempt to bring the classic heist movie genre into the 2020s in its presentation (and political message), just like war of the worlds attempted (poorly) to update that classic sci-fi story with amazon drones and ice cube responding to text messages for an entire movie. Caroline Siede, writing for Decoding Everything, says:.

How to Rob a Bank wants to be a rallying cry for social revolution via internet community building, but it winds up feeling more like a mindless TikTok scroll.

Diungkapkan bahwa even the more positive reviews, like cortlyn kelly's 2. 5-star review for Roger Ebert, call attention to this:.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, breaking the silver-screen barrier, the ringleader, ryan (hoult), addresses his audience by stating how important they are; almost like a double entendre, the movie speaks to both its fictional audience and those in the theater. This focus on the audience is intriguing, adding depth to an otherwise standard money-heist flick. Pandering to a younger generation by contentifying the plot makes it easy for ‘How to Rob a Bank’ to one day be screened as a 212-part TikTok series.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the same can be said for the positive-ish review from the hollywood reporter, which is pretty harsh on the social media aspects of the film. Writer David Rooney says:.

While the robberies are diverting enough and the YouTube inserts splashed with pop-up graphics, the fun wears a bit thin, which makes the shift into trauma and pathos a welcome one, even if the transition might have been smoother.

The Globe and Mail’s review of How to Rob a Bank also questions the presentation of the movie in social media form, with film critic Radheyan Simonpillai writing:.

Berdasarkan laporan, this is not a heist movie. It’s the online hack to a heist movie, curiously made for the big screen, seeking the path of least resistance to constant dopamine hits. We’re foregoing all the labour of a heist movie because it would likely be oh so tedious for the movie’s target audience, presumably the generation under 30, whose work ethic is constantly called into question.

The fact that How to Rob A Bank also tried to make an anti-establishment, anti-banking movie while being financed by Amazon isn’t helping its case, per some reviews.

For example, in his 2-star review for The Guardian, Benjamin Lee wrote that not only does the movie feel like it was put together by someone trying to nail the “right now” of social media and missing badly, but the political message is also lost:.

It’s a little hard to stomach an anti-capitalism screed not only funded by Amazon but featuring several scenes of lame, please-aim-logo-towards-camera, product placement (after one dismantles the system, a refreshing can of Mountain Dew really does hit the spot).

Writing for The Daily Beast, Nick Schager puts the film’s attempt at a political statement even more succinctly:.

Their film attempts to rage against the machine from within the (Amazon/MGM) machine.

Diungkapkan bahwa in fact, amazon and its ceo, jeff bezos, find themselves at the heart of a lot of the negative reviews. William Bibbiani at The Wrap writes:.

Sebagaimana diketahui, it’s an amazon-mgm production, which makes the film’s efforts to sell anti-capitalism as entertainment hypocritical, laughable and insulting. It’s a film that says you should stand up to Jeff Bezos, but only after you pay Jeff Bezos. No matter how cool “Atomic Blonde” director David Leitch tries to make bank robbing look, this is the opposite of cool.

Berdasarkan laporan, i would like to note that not all of the reviews are scathing, but none are overwhelmingly positive, either. The movie seems like it delivers on action for many reviews (though some didn’t like it), but the great action sequences don’t seem to save it from itself, even if some reviews found How to Rob a Bank fun enough.

Berdasarkan laporan, the movie also doesn’t look like it’ll be all that big of a hit at the box office, meaning it’ll likely be available to watch with a prime subscription pretty quickly. We’ll have to see on that.

Sebagaimana diketahui, more information and a star-studded cast list have dropped for hulu's revival of the circle, and i'm still as hyped as i was when it was first announced. The newest iteration kicks off on the 2026 TV schedule on November 17th, but the season has already technically begun. Netflix's version of the original series was solid, but I think these changes may just push it into the conversation about the best reality TV shows. Here's who we can expect to compete in this season, as well as more on the fan vote people can already take part in.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the circle is already shaking things up by taking a page out of what many reality shows are doing lately by bringing in other reality stars from other shows. This series didn't hold back with some heavy hitters, bringing in The Bachelor's Hannah Brown and DWTS alum Sasha Farber, as well as some others amidst its civilian players. Take a look at the full lineup:.

Berdasarkan laporan, brown is a great pick as far as reality show vets go, and i support the circle taking a page from the traitors in welcoming on a dancing with the stars pro. I also love that Dominic is going to be catfishing the contestants by posing as Lisa Vanderpump, and I'm also wondering how he can possibly make that work. I guess when people are hiding behind a screen, they can pull a lot of tricks.

Berdasarkan laporan, while the circle will continue with its general premise of contestants staying in separate apartments and only interacting via a chat app, there are some unique twists in store for this season. One is that fans can vote on what happens and impact how the season unfolds. A vote is already underway where readers can decide which identity Layla Taylor and Kate Rackner will play under.

6 Ways Netflix's The Circle Is The Perfect Big Brother Substitute.

Berdasarkan laporan, the fan vote is huge because, frankly, fans love to vote. Having influence over the game from home can lead to unpredictability, which is a cornerstone of entertaining reality television.

Diungkapkan bahwa that alone has me sold, but let's not forget what having a fan vote also means. It means this season will be unfolding in real time, whereas previous seasons of The Circle were filmed months before a single episode even aired. As someone who is often glued to Big Brother's live feeds during its run, I can't wait to tune in with my Hulu subscription and see how my vote impacts the game, maybe just a day after that vote gets placed.

Diungkapkan bahwa i've been dying for a new reality show to watch, and i feel like my wish has been granted! here's hoping the circle lives up to the hype and becomes the next reality obsession. I would love to have another late-Fall show to add to my lineup, especially with the winter months approaching!.
